item.redstonecircuit.redstone_goggles.fi: (Redstone goggles fitted: the same effect as wearing them)
item.redstonecircuit.frequency_tuner.tip: Binds sync torches into one channel

Right-click a sync torch: with no channel in hand, take the one it already has; with one in hand, join it (moved over if it sat on another); with neither, start a new channel. Shift-right-click clears that torch's channel, or the hand's channel when the torch has none
block.redstonecircuit.retaining_repeater: A repeater that hands on the strength it was given instead of restoring fifteen
Right-click: cycles 1-4 like vanilla (2 ticks each); input at the front, output at the back; in 7 means out 7
block.redstonecircuit.double_repeater.ti: A repeater whose every delay setting lasts twice as long
Right-click: cycles 1-4 (4 / 8 / 12 / 16 ticks, vanilla is 2 / 4 / 6 / 8); input at the front, output at the back, restored to fifteen
block.redstonecircuit.double_retaining_r: Twice the delay, and the strength that arrives is the strength that leaves
Right-click: cycles 1-4 (4 / 8 / 12 / 16 ticks); input at the front, output at the back; in 7 means out 7
block.redstonecircuit.weather_detector.t: Holds a signal while the weather matches its setting
Right-click: clear -> rain (no thunder) -> thunder -> clear; always fifteen; needs no view of the sky
block.redstonecircuit.transformer.tip: Answers from its back at the strength you set, whatever arrives at its front; nothing at the front means 0
block.redstonecircuit.transformer.tip.de: Right-click: the control screen - the output strength 1-15 is in there; front in, back out
block.redstonecircuit.clock.tip: Emits the strength you set from its back once every (seconds x 20 + ticks), for the 1 or 2 ticks you set; 0 seconds 0 ticks is off
block.redstonecircuit.clock.tip.detail: Right-click: the control screen - seconds 0-3600, ticks 0-19, strength 1-15, pulse 1-2 ticks; the front faces you, the back emits
block.redstonecircuit.extender.tip: Answers its input as it is, and keeps answering it for the set time after the input leaves
block.redstonecircuit.extender.tip.detai: Right-click: the control screen - seconds 0-3600, ticks 0-19; the front is the input, the back the output; 0 seconds 0 ticks extends nothing
block.redstonecircuit.sync_torch.tip: Lights while the face it is mounted on is powered; every torch on one channel lights and goes dark together
block.redstonecircuit.trigger.tip: One pulse flips it on or off
block.redstonecircuit.trigger.tip.detail: Reads its front face, answers 15 from its back while on
block.redstonecircuit.sync_torch.tip.det: The shape and faces of a redstone torch with the polarity reversed: input on the mounting face, full strength on the other five; an unbound torch is a group of one, and tuning several to one channel is what makes them move together
block.redstonecircuit.redstone_structure: Right-click: the editor - show, confirm and apply are all in there
A capture is held in the block until a release uses it
block.redstonecircuit.logic_integrator.t: A logic gate with seven modes
Right-click: the control screen - the gate and the two strengths X and Y are in there
block.redstonecircuit.block_placer.tip: Places the blocks in its box out of the front
block.redstonecircuit.block_placer.tip.d: Right-click: the dispenser's own nine-slot window; one redstone signal places one block out of the front (blocks only)
Lets the main input through while exactly one side input signals
Front: main input. Back: main output. The other four faces are side inputs: with exactly one of them signalling, the back emits the main input's strength; with none or more than one, it emits nothing
block.redstonecircuit.controller.tip: Compares the signal at its front against the input level, and answers from its back while the condition holds
block.redstonecircuit.controller.tip.det: Right-click: the control screen - main level (greater/less), sub level (equal/not equal/only equal/only not equal), input level 0-15 and output strength 1-15 are in there
block.redstonecircuit.structure.tip.deta: Put down by 红石结构方块's releases; useless in hand, it only lives inside a structure

item.redstonecircuit.redstone_goggles.ti: Worn on the head: blocks holding redstone become translucent and show what is inside
You can see the shape, facing, delay and wiring of the redstone inside a block
Craft with any helmet (crafting table or the 2x2 grid): that helmet stays itself, keeps its enchantments and damage, and gains the goggles' effect
The redstone wrench needs them to be worn
item.redstonecircuit.superconducting_red: Redstone that does not lose strength
Like redstone: right-click to lay it on a block, shift-right-click to put it inside one
No signal loss: it carries its full strength however far it goes
item.redstonecircuit.redstone_wrench.tip: Right-click redstone to pick it as A
Shift-right-click a neighbour B (a piston, a lamp, any block - it needs no redstone of its own) to lock that line and cut every other side; repeat to step through lock / cut / auto
item.redstonecircuit.rotation_rod.tip: Steps a component's orientation round a fixed cycle
item.redstonecircuit.rotation_rod.tip.in: Right-click a block holding redstone: each click turns it 90 degrees clockwise (north, east, south, west)
item.redstonecircuit.rotation_rod.tip.ou: After a full turn it goes up, then down, then back to north for the next round
item.redstonecircuit.rotation_rod.tip.wi: Dust has no direction, so the rod has nothing to turn

redstonecircuit.configuration.title: Redstone Circuit Configs
redstonecircuit.configuration.validateHo: A block may only hold redstone if it is a full, opaque cube. Turn this off to allow any block (debug and creative only).
redstonecircuit.configuration.debugLog.t: Log every placement and retrieval, including refused ones, to the game log.
redstonecircuit.configuration.allowRepla: Shift-right-clicking a block that already holds a component replaces it. Off means a second placement falls through to vanilla.
redstonecircuit.configuration.placerCrea: Let the block placer create a standalone one-block structure when it is itself physical. On by default; turned off, the placement is refused and nothing is spent.
redstonecircuit.configuration.hostOverla: When the host block is drawn as a translucent framed cube: GOGGLES only while the goggles are worn, ALWAYS, or OFF for no overlay.
Opacity of the shell, 0-255. Around 150 reads as frosted glass; 0 draws the border only.
Shell colour as RRGGBB hex; a leading '#' is allowed.
Opacity of the border drawn around each face of the shell, 0-255. 0 draws the shell without a border.
Border colour as RRGGBB hex; a leading '#' is allowed.
redstonecircuit.configuration.supercondu: Border colour for a block holding superconducting wire, as RRGGBB hex. Set it equal to the border colour above to drop the distinction.
redstonecircuit.configuration.hostAccept: A host block is powered by the strong power a neighbouring solid block carries, as in vanilla. Off means only blocks that emit a signal themselves can feed it.
redstonecircuit.configuration.hostConduc: Host blocks pass strong power on
Whether a host block passes on the strong power a neighbouring diode pushes into it. Off keeps power at the component inside.
redstonecircuit.configuration.showInnerC: Draw the component inside the block
Draw the component itself inside the shell, so a wire, a repeater's facing and a lit torch can be read from outside the block.
redstonecircuit.configuration.seeInnerCo: Draw the component even when a solid block is in the way. Off, so the effect never becomes X-ray vision.
redstonecircuit.configuration.forceOverl: DEBUG. Draw the shell and the component for every known host, ignoring the colour and visibility settings. Appearance mode OFF still draws nothing.
redstonecircuit.configuration.wrenchNeed: Require the redstone goggles to be worn before the wrench will do anything. On by default.
redstonecircuit.configuration.wrenchClea: Shift-right-clicking the block already selected with the wrench clears its connection overrides, so it goes back to automatic behaviour.
redstonecircuit.configuration.rotationRo: Require the redstone goggles to be worn before the rotation rod will turn anything. On by default, like the wrench.
redstonecircuit.configuration.innerAdjus: Changing something inside a block requires the goggles
Require the redstone goggles before a bare hand can change a setting inside a block - a delay, a mode. Levers and buttons are exempt, and a refusal is silent.
redstonecircuit.configuration.traceSlotS: Log every component update sent to clients. Very noisy while a circuit runs; it answers whether the client is told about a block at all.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carrierEna: Let inner components travel with the Create contraption or Sable sub-level that picks their block up. Off leaves them behind at their world position.
redstonecircuit.configuration.traceCarri: Log every contraption callback, including the ones that carry nothing. One line per block of a machine.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carrierFre: Carried components ignore the world they fly through
Close the bridge between a carried component and the world it is flying through. Off by default, so a machine lights the redstone it passes over.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carrierStr: Read the signals the structure carries
Let the redstone inside a moving structure read the signal sources the structure itself is carrying. Off reads only the world outside.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carrierNot: Also notify the neighbours of a carried host's own structure coordinate when its output changes. Off notifies only the projected world position.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carrierBlo: Breaking a carried block drops the component
Drop the component as an item when a block a structure is carrying is broken, as in the world. It never fires for a release or a landing.
redstonecircuit.configuration.adoptWorld: Adopt world components into the structure
Migrate a component in the world's own store at a moving structure's own coordinate into that structure's record. This repairs a save that already has such an entry.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carrierSel: Blocks the self-healing sweep checks per tick
How many blocks riding a moving structure the self-healing sweep may examine per tick. 0 turns it off.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carrierWor: The world reads the carried host's output
Let the redstone inside an ordinary block read the output of a host a structure is carrying, at the world position that host occupies.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carriedWre: Let the redstone wrench be used on a host block a moving structure is carrying: pick it, then shift-click a neighbour. Off leaves a carried host untouched.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carriedRot: Rotation rod works on carried blocks
Let the rotation rod be used on a host block a moving structure is carrying: click a face to make it the input side, again for the output side.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carriedIns: Let a component be put into a block a moving structure is carrying, and taken back out again. Turn it off first if placing into a carried block misbehaves.
Handle a coordinate a moving structure owns on the carrier side before the world's own click handling. Turn it off first if a click on a carried block misbehaves.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carriedSwi: A bare hand works carried switches
Let a bare hand work a component inside a block a moving structure is carrying: flick a lever, step a delay, swap a mode. Buttons are not included.
redstonecircuit.configuration.verboseSol: Log every individual solver step. Very noisy: one tick of an ordinary build can produce hundreds of lines.
redstonecircuit.configuration.verboseRen: Log the client's carried-render diagnostics every frame instead of only when the picture changes. It never changes what is drawn.
redstonecircuit.configuration.solverSpin: How many times one host may be recomputed inside a single tick before a solver spin warning names it. Only a defective circuit reaches this.
redstonecircuit.configuration.solverCoal: Coalesce the solver's neighbour notifications to the tick boundary, so the solver cannot re-feed itself inside one tick. Off sends one notification per change.
redstonecircuit.configuration.solverCasc: How many solve-then-notify passes one tick may run, so the world's reaction to those notifications is absorbed in the same tick. 1 turns the cascade off, which is exactly the behaviour without it. The adaptive backoff is built in and not a setting: a dimension whose last tick did not converge gets half its budget, so a clock that genuinely oscillates costs what it costs today while a converging machine keeps the whole budget.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carriedJad: Let Jade show the component hidden inside a block a moving structure is carrying, as it does for a world block.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carrierPos: How long, in ticks, a moving structure's pose stays trustworthy on the client. Past this age the client stops drawing the component inside it, so keep it well above the heartbeat.
How often, in ticks, the server re-sends the pose of every structure that is holding something, moved or not. It is what lets the client tell a parked machine from one that has gone away.
How often, in ticks, the server re-sends the pose of a structure holding something while it may be turning. 0 disables sampling.
redstonecircuit.configuration.carrierSol: Solve the redstone inside moving structures
Recompute the redstone inside a moving structure from its own local layout. Off leaves every component at the value it had when the block was picked up.
How many components one structure may settle in a single tick. A ceiling on work, not on machine size: the rest keeps settling over the following ticks.
How many of one structure's host blocks may be used as a starting point for a solve, per tick. The remaining hosts are solved over the following ticks.
redstonecircuit.configuration.traceCarri: Log one line per pass for every structure that has components riding it. It prints once a tick.
redstonecircuit.configuration.slotSyncRa: How far component updates reach, in blocks. 0 sends them to everyone in the dimension. 0 is the safe default: a client that misses an update keeps drawing the old state.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureM: The longest axis a captured structure may have, in blocks; 48 is vanilla's own structure block limit. The load budget is counted from it.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureP: How large the downsampled preview that travels with a structure may be, in bytes. Keep it well below the game's 1 MiB payload cap.
How many cells the downsampled preview may have, as a volume - not how many are filled. Together with the size budget it decides the preview's scale; the coarser of the two wins.
Emit a structure preview's geometry once and redraw it, instead of rebuilding the miniature every frame. Turn it off if a preview crashes or draws wrongly.
Drop the cells of a structure preview that are completely buried inside it. Turn it off to draw every cell, which tells a culling problem from a sampling one.
Leave out the faces of a structure preview that the cell behind them hides. Turn it off to draw every face, which tells a face-culling problem from a sampling one.
Draw a structure at half resolution wherever it is drawn as an icon (hand, slot, ground). Turn it off to draw the full picture everywhere.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureC: Snapshot the one block of world around a selection when capturing it. The shell travels into the plot but is never written into the payload or released.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureM: How far from a structure a player may be and still press its manual keys, in blocks. Measured from the player's eyes and checked by the server on every press.
How long one press pushes, in ticks. A press is a pulse, never a hold, so it cannot be left running. 10 ticks is enough for a repeater, a piston or a dispenser.
The least number of ticks between two accepted presses from one player. It keeps a held or spammed key from driving a machine at tick speed.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureI: The least number of ticks between two changes of the signal a structure injects into one cell of its plot. A change that arrives too soon is held and let through when its window opens.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureM: How many chunk columns may be held loaded by structures at once, counted in columns, never structures. A structure that does not fit is asleep: it still exists and can be released, but is not ticked.
How many structures may be ticked at once, whatever their size. Checked together with the column budget: both have to allow a structure before it ticks.
How many entries the manual-mode panel may hold in one structure.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureP: Keep the pocket dimension's time and weather equal to the overworld's, so a weather detector or a daylight-dependent block reads what it read where it stood.
Play pocket sounds where the structure stands

Play the sounds a captured structure makes where the structure stands. The blocks inside a structure run in the hidden pocket dimension, where no player ever is, so a note block or a lever in there was silent.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureA: Allow the copying tier at all. It copies container contents along with the blocks, so a chest of items is duplicated too. Creative mode only.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureM: How many structures deep a capture may go. 1 means a structure may hold another structure, but not a third. 0 forbids any structure block inside a capture.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureB: Blocks that may not be captured
Block ids that may not be captured. Bedrock, the portals and the command blocks are here because a captured one can be released anywhere. An unknown id is logged and skipped.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureM: Carry inner components with a structure
Carry this mod's own components that live inside blocks with a captured structure, and put them back on release. Without it a captured host block arrives empty inside.
redstonecircuit.configuration.structureR: Ask before a release overwrites blocks
Ask before a release overwrites blocks: a target holding anything is refused once, with the block count, and goes ahead when asked again.
Blocks written per tick on release
How many blocks a release writes per tick. A 48-cubed structure is 110,592 blocks, too many for one tick; 4096 is about 27 ticks for the largest allowed structure.
block.redstonecircuit.honey_piston.tip: Pushes like a piston; on retracting, if the cell ahead is air, it drags one block back
block.redstonecircuit.honey_piston.tip.d: Only on retraction: pushing never drags, and pushing a block never drags
